they should depose him,
because his character was not suitable for kingship,
and they should seat you upon the royal throne of the house of Magog.
Then Ghazan sent word to Baydu, saying:
"You are the great one in Israel,
and all of us together submit to you,
and we conduct ourselves according to your leadership.
Whatever you know is fitting, right, and useful, do it,
provided only that without harm and without commotion the foundations {OCR?} of our kingdom remain firm.
And whoever is chosen,
it is not in profligacy, eating, drinking, boastings, and luxuries that he ought to indulge himself, nor in lavish gifts given unjustly,
but he should guard his kingdom with vigilance,
and continually consider how he may meet his enemies;
because by the wisdom of a king, more than by tens of thousands of warriors, a kingdom is preserved."
Then the grandees, the sons of the kings, and the commanders of tens of thousands of the Mongols, when they were assured
that Ghazan and Baydu were in agreement,
and were acting with one accord and one will lovingly toward each other,
and were communicating by means of envoys,
and it was evident to them
that their law justified Ghazan having the royal throne after Gaykhatu,
and that Baydu was fighting in order to seat Ghazan upon the royal throne,
cheerfully submitted to Baydu.
And they turned their faces away from Gaykhatu without his noticing,
and he did not know what was going on in the world,
but was indulging himself greatly in worldly lusts, until the matter was revealed to those inside and outside.
Then he awoke as if from sleep,
and sent an envoy toward the north,
so that the armies there might mount up
and seize Baydu.
And when the envoy reached the northern region,
that is, the land of Diyarbakr,
he found that all the armies there had joined Baydu,
and were about to go and attack Gaykhatu.
And as if in secret, that envoy slipped away and fled back,
and went and informed Gaykhatu of their intention.
And as soon as he heard these things,
he supposed that Baydu was about to flee and go to Ghazan;
he sent troops and seized the roads and mountain passes (kleisourai) of Khorasan.
And he also mounted Taghar, the great general, with ten thousand men,
and sent him... {OCR?}
... toward the region {OCR?}.
